items.title: Google AI Mode updates recipe results to better connect people with recipe creators
items.summary: Google updated AI Mode for recipe searches to include links to recipe sites and more details like cook time, addressing traffic concerns from creators. This aims to drive more clicks back to original content amid AI summaries. It signals a trend toward balancing AI answers with publisher traffic.

items.title: Google’s AI Mode is citing Google more than any other site: Study
items.summary: Google’s AI Mode cites Google.com 17.42% of the time, up significantly, often linking to its own search results. This self-preferencing may reduce external traffic, urging SEO alignment with Google's ecosystem. It underscores shifts in AI citation dynamics across industries.

items.title: Penguin Michael Joseph Signs Multi-Book Deal with Self-Published Thriller Author Lucinda Berry
items.summary: Penguin Michael Joseph has acquired world rights to a new thriller, The Golden Child, by formerly self-published author Lucinda Berry, marking her transition to traditional publishing in the UK and Commonwealth. Berry, known for her popular psychological thrillers, will continue her publishing journey with PMJ. This deal highlights the growing interest in self-pub success stories securing major contracts.

items.title: Humans Beat AI in Storytelling Contest Offering Publishing Contract Prize
items.summary: A writing contest pitting human authors against AI-generated stories concluded with humans winning top prizes, including a publishing contract for first place. Judges preferred human entries for depth and originality despite AI's efficiency. The event underscores ongoing debates about AI's role in creative writing and publishing.

items.title: NYT Spotlights Generative AI Controversy in Indie Author Space
items.summary: A New York Times article highlighted growing controversies around indie authors using generative AI for content creation, sparking debates on ethics and quality. Indie Author Magazine discusses agentic AI advancements and potential legal ripples affecting publishing practices. Authors are urged to adapt while building independent business foundations amid platform disruptions.

items.title: Gaming Publication Network Fires Staff, Replaces with AI-Generated Writers
items.summary: Clickout Media, owning sites like The Escapist and Videogamer, sacked up to 20 journalists and substituted them with fictitious AI writers complete with fake bios and photos. Staff trained the AI amid budget cuts, leading to controversies including removed fake reviews. This incident raises alarms about AI deception in content publishing.

items.title: Geological Society Issues Guidelines for Responsible AI Use in Scholarly Publishing
items.summary: The Geological Society supports AI tools in research but mandates disclosure of AI use in writing, analysis, or images, prohibiting AI authorship. Reviewers must verify AI-assisted work without uploading confidential content to LLMs. The policy emphasizes human oversight and content integrity amid AI's rise.

items.title: BookTok Trends Feature Emerald Fennell's Wuthering Heights, Reviving Canonical Classics
items.summary: BookTok creators are buzzing about director Emerald Fennell's adaptation of Wuthering Heights, driving interest in the classic novel and prompting discussions on returning to traditional literature. The platform highlights trending genres and timeless titles amid viral content. This surge underscores BookTok's influence on reading canonical works.

items.title: Pixar's 'Hoppers' Dominates Box Office While Maggie Gyllenhaal's 'The Bride!' Struggles
items.summary: Pixar's latest animated film 'Hoppers' led the global box office with an impressive $88 million opening weekend debut. In contrast, Maggie Gyllenhaal's 'The Bride!' underperformed, earning only $13 million worldwide amid reports of flatlining performance. The divergent results highlight varying audience reception to recent releases.

items.title: Rosanna Arquette Criticizes Quentin Tarantino's Use of N-Word in Films
items.summary: Rosanna Arquette, known for her role in Pulp Fiction, blasted Quentin Tarantino for using the N-word in his movies, calling it racist and creepy rather than artistic. She claimed he has been given a 'hall pass' for it. The comments reignite ongoing debates about language in Hollywood films.

items.title: Harry Styles Surprises During Ryan Gosling's 'SNL' Monologue
items.summary: Harry Styles made an unexpected cameo during Ryan Gosling's 'Saturday Night Live' opening monologue, which featured an alien-themed skit tied to Gosling's upcoming project. The surprise appearance added to the episode's buzz. Fans celebrated the pop culture crossover moment.

items.title: Timothée Chalamet Faces Backlash from Ballet and Opera Communities Over Dismissive Comments
items.summary: Timothée Chalamet sparked outrage from ballet and opera enthusiasts after saying during a town hall that he doesn't want theaters to become like those arts, where 'no one cares' despite efforts to sustain them. The remarks were mocked on SNL's Weekend Update. The backlash underscores sensitivities around cultural appreciation.

items.title: 'Scary Movie' Trailer Draws Woke Backlash Over Pronoun Joke
items.summary: The trailer for the new 'Scary Movie' film featured a pronoun joke, prompting strong reactions from critics accusing it of insensitivity. Supporters hailed it as a return to the franchise's irreverent humor. The controversy highlights divides in audience expectations for comedy.

items.title: Anna Camp Apologizes After Reposting Scream 7 Boycott Failure Story
items.summary: Scream 7 star Anna Camp faced criticism for reposting a story claiming the film's boycott and critic hate 'didn't work,' prompting her to delete it and issue an apology stating it doesn't reflect her beliefs. The incident stems from calls to boycott the movie over various issues. It illustrates tensions around celebrity social media engagement.

items.title: Small Business Technology News: Intuit Launches AI-Powered ERP Solution Tailored For Construction Industry
items.summary: Intuit has launched a new Construction Edition for its Intuit Enterprise Suite, an AI-native ERP solution designed to support mid-market construction companies by combining project, financial, and operational workflows in one system. Key features include AI-powered processes and industry-specific tools such as cost proposals, invoicing, and budgeting. This offering provides a scalable path for construction businesses growing out of QuickBooks, potentially simplifying their accounting system upgrades.

items.title: AI Infrastructure for Small Businesses: How To Prepare Without Overcommitting
items.summary: Small businesses do not require hyperscale AI infrastructure to leverage AI effectively; instead, they can achieve meaningful results through smart planning, rightsized investments, and focusing on one or two high-value opportunities with low implementation time. An AI readiness assessment and workshops help translate vague directives into actionable roadmaps, identifying necessary data, technologies, and infrastructure levels. While cloud-based AI offers simplicity for quick experimentation, on-prem options provide cost predictability, better performance, and control, especially with modern hardware like entry-level GPUs, allowing businesses to experiment without overspending.
